definitions.explanation: A period in Japanese prehistory characterized by the introduction of wet-rice agriculture, bronze and iron tools, and new pottery styles. Named after the Yayoi district in Tokyo where distinctive pottery was first discovered.

examples.japanese: {弥生時代|やよいじだい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{稲作|いなさく}→稲作：09494_inasaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{伝|つた}わった→伝わる：01961_tsutawaru⟧。
examples.english: Rice cultivation was introduced during the Yayoi period.

examples.japanese: {弥生時代|やよいじだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{遺跡|いせき}→遺跡：09527_iseki⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{銅鏡|どうきょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出土|しゅつど}→出土：11760_shutsudo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Bronze mirrors were excavated from a Yayoi period archaeological site.

examples.japanese: {弥生時代|やよいじだい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{縄文時代|じょうもんじだい}→縄文時代：18895_joumonjidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{続|つづ}く→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{社会|しゃかい}→社会：01427_shakai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大|おお}きく→大きい：00335_ookii⟧⟦{変化|へんか}した→変化する：20997_henkasuru⟧。
examples.english: The Yayoi period followed the Jomon period and was a time of great social change in Japan.

notes:
Named after {弥生|やよい}{町|ちょう} in {文京区|ぶんきょうく}, Tokyo, where a distinctive type of pottery was discovered in 1884. This period saw revolutionary changes in Japanese society with the arrival of wet-rice agriculture from the Asian continent.

KEY FEATURES:
- ⟦{稲作|いなさく}→稲作：09494_inasaku⟧ (wet-rice farming) was introduced from the Korean peninsula and China
- {青銅器|せいどうき} (bronze tools) and {鉄器|てっき} (iron tools) came into use
- Settled agricultural communities replaced the earlier hunter-gatherer lifestyle
- Social stratification and early political structures began to form

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {弥生時代|やよいじだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{遺跡|いせき}→遺跡：09527_iseki⟧: Yayoi period archaeological site
- {弥生時代|やよいじだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{土器|どき}→土器：09658_doki⟧: Yayoi pottery
- ⟦{弥生|やよい}→弥生：20353_yayoi⟧⟦{文化|ぶんか}→文化：01504_bunka⟧: Yayoi culture

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{縄文時代|じょうもんじだい}→縄文時代：18895_joumonjidai⟧: Jomon period — the preceding period of hunter-gatherer culture
- ⟦{古墳時代|こふんじだい}→古墳時代：23333_kofunjidai⟧: Kofun period — the following period of keyhole-shaped burial mounds
